segments.spokenText: Part 2. Welcome to the riverside craft fair. You now have one minute to read questions 11 to 20.

Welcome to our annual riverside craft fair. Before you explore, I'll explain the site and mention a few changes to the programme. Please keep the printed plan facing the way you entered: the gate is at the bottom and the river at the top. The main path runs straight from the gate towards the river. The letters on the plan mark places, not the names of activities. We have kept the central crossing clear so visitors can move between the two sides without walking through a stall queue.

Please keep the printed plan facing the way you entered: the gate is at the bottom and the river at the top. The main path runs straight from the gate towards the river. The letters on the plan mark places, not the names of activities. We have kept the central crossing clear so visitors can move between the two sides without walking through a stall queue.

segments.spokenText: The information tent is the first place on your left as you come through the gate. You can leave a message there if you become separated from someone. Directly opposite it, on the right-hand side of the entrance path, is the bag store. Please don't confuse the two. We can keep a coat or shopping bag in the store, but valuables should stay with you. There is no charge, though everything must be collected before we close.

segments.spokenText: Continue up the path to the crossing. The pottery demonstrations are on the left, in the middle row of the plan. The demonstrators need water, which is why they aren't using the dry space near the gate this year. Across the path in the same row is the repair stall. Bring a small household object there and the volunteers will discuss what might be possible. They cannot promise to complete every repair during the fair, but can often identify the next useful step.

segments.spokenText: At the far end, beside the river, you'll find the quiet seating area. It's the space on the left, not the performance platform on the right. We've kept music away from that seating because some visitors want somewhere to rest and talk without raising their voices. The central space nearest the river is being kept empty for access, and it isn't an extra picnic area.

segments.spokenText: Now, about today's arrangements. The fair has been moved from Sunday to Saturday this year because the riverside road will be used for a running event tomorrow. It wasn't a change caused by the weather forecast, and it has nothing to do with the availability of the makers. Most have reserved both dates anyway. We hope announcing it early has prevented wasted journeys.

segments.spokenText: There will be a small admission charge for the evening music, but entrance to the craft fair itself is free. The money from the music will pay for next year's sign-language interpretation. We had considered buying more display tables, but accessibility support was the priority chosen at our last public meeting.

segments.spokenText: For children, there is a short weaving workshop. Parents sometimes expect to leave children there while they shop. This time an adult must stay with each child, since the activity is designed for them to work together. You don't need to reserve, but if a table is full you'll be asked to return at the next starting time rather than stand in the working area.

segments.spokenText: We ask stallholders to avoid disposable packaging where possible. Visitors can help by bringing containers for small purchases. There is a recycling point near the gate, but using fewer packages is our first aim; the recycling bins aren't a reason to wrap everything twice. Some delicate pieces do need protection, and makers will explain the options.

segments.spokenText: Finally, if you have comments about the fair, please use the short paper form at the information tent. We will post an online survey next week, but today's form asks about routes and seating while they're fresh in your mind. There's no prize draw attached. We want to hear about a difficulty even if the rest of your visit was enjoyable. Thank you, and have a good afternoon.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 2. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
